extracted.intended_audience: Grantees and institutional officials (PD/PIs, SOs, AOs, delegates) using eRA Commons to prepare and submit RPPRs
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step guidance and procedural requirements for preparing, editing, validating, routing, and submitting the Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) in eRA Commons, including agency-specific notes for NIH, AHRQ, VA, DOC, SBIR/STTR, and multi-component awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Participants - purpose and S/K flag
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR Section D. lets the agency know who has worked on the project to gauge and report performance in promoting partnerships and collaborations. S/K in the list of participants stands for Senior/Key, meaning is the participant a senior or key personnel on the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read all onscreen instructions before completing this form. Onscreen instructions for D.1 vary slightly between research, training, and complex awards. See the RPPR Instruction Guide for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. Impact - describe project impact during reporting period
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR Section E Impact will be used to describe ways in which the work, findings, and specific products of the project have had an impact during this reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the RPPR Instruction Guide for details of how to fill this form out.

rubrics_metrics.name: F. Changes - prior approval for significant changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR Section F addresses Changes. Recipients are reminded that significant changes in objectives and scope require prior approval of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form (Section F) is not required for Final or Interim RPPRs. See the RPPR Instruction Guide for details of how to fill this form out.

rubrics_metrics.name: G. Special Reporting Requirements - agency-specific terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR Section G Special Reporting Requirements address agency-specific award terms and conditions, as well as any award specific reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the question regarding the SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure Form in G.1 appears only for SBIR/STTR awards and only after the award has undergone due diligence. Agency-specific applicability notes (e.g., DOC: Sections G.2, G.3, and G.13 are not applicable) appear on the form. See RPPR Instruction Guide for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: H. Budget - when required and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: This form lets you add a budget to the RPPR. The Budget form is not required for Final or Interim RPPRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the RPPR Instruction Guide for details of how to fill this form out. For assistance with information required on the forms, refer to the Application Guide and navigate to the R&R Budget Form topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget form types (SF424 R&R, PHS 398 Training, PHS Additional Indirect Costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most awards now use the SF424 R&R budget form. However, training awards may use the SF424 and/or the PHS 398 training budget. The PHS Additional Indirect Costs budget form is available as an optional form for the Overall component of a multi-project award with multiple institutions/organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please contact the Grants Management Specialist assigned to your grant if you have questions on the appropriate form to use. Agency-specific exceptions noted (e.g., DOC requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding a budget - UI actions
rubrics_metrics.description: To add a budget, choose an option from the drop-down list and click the Add Budget button. The added budget type appears in the first table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Edit option under the three-dot ellipsis icon to open the form for editing. Click the Save button before exiting the form. NOTE: You can delete a budget that you added by clicking its three-dot ellipsis icon and selecting Delete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward budgets (H.2) - adding and deleting
rubrics_metrics.description: To add a subaward budget, choose an option from the drop-down list and click the Add Subaward Budget button. The added budget type appears in the second table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Edit option under the three-dot ellipsis icon to open the form for editing. Click the Save button before exiting the form. Subaward budget types include SF424 Research & Related Subaward Budget and PHS 398 Subaward Training Budget. NOTE: You can delete a subaward budget you added via the three-dot ellipsis Delete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of completed subaward budgets on main budget F.5
rubrics_metrics.description: If subaward budgets are completed, the system will not calculate the budget line item F.5 for the main budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total consortium costs for the main budget MUST be computed and entered manually into budget line item F.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) / Organization Name behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: For single component RPPRs, the grantee's UEI and organization name automatically populate the Unique Entity Identifier and Organization Name fields of the budget form and cannot be edited. For multi-component RPPRs, the UEI and Organization Name fields are prepopulated based on the overall component but can be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change for multi-component budgets: Edit the budget, click the magnifying glass next to the UEI or Organization Name to open Search Organization popup, search or Add New Organization (enter UEI and org name and Save). Both fields are required to be populated.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF424 Research & Related Budget - source of required information
rubrics_metrics.description: For assistance with the information required on the SF424 Research & Related Budget form, refer to the Application Guide and the R&R Budget Form topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific note: The How to Apply - Application Guide does not apply to DOC awards; however the SF424 Research and Related Budget form is required for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF424 Research & Related Subaward Budget - source of required information
rubrics_metrics.description: For assistance with the information required on the SF424 Research & Related Subaward Budget form, refer to the Application Guide and the R&R Subaward Budget topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific note: The How to Apply - Application Guide does not apply to DOC awards; however the SF424 Research & Related Subaward Budget form may be required for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Training Budget - source of required information
rubrics_metrics.description: For assistance with the information required on the PHS 398 Training Budget, refer to the Application Guide and navigate to the PHS Training Budget topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific note: This form is not applicable to DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: I. Outcomes - Final RPPR requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The I. Outcomes form is used to provide information regarding the cumulative outcomes or findings of the project. This form is applicable only to Final RPPRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the RPPR Instruction Guide for details of how to fill this form out. Agency-specific note: DOC may not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: J. Misc. Documents - upload limits and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This form lets you upload up to 25 files with sizes of up to 6MB each to be submitted with your RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-specific instructions: This form appears for Department of Commerce (DOC) awards only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing RPPR for editing - initial status and editor roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an RPPR is initiated, its status becomes PD/PI Work in Progress and it becomes available for editing for the PI who initiated it. The PD/PI or delegate uses the Edit option for viewing and completing the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RPPR is routed by the PI to another user (such as an SO or AO), then that user becomes the current reviewer and can edit the RPPR. NOTE: For RPPRs with multiple PD/PIs (MPI awards), only the Contact PD/PI has access to Edit unless the Contact PD/PI has granted progress report authority to other PD/PIs. Without this authority, MPIs can only view the RPPR PDF and its routing history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two ways to access RPPR for editing
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two means of accessing the progress report for editing: (1) Access RPPR from the Status module via List of Applications/Grants and click RPPR link, or (2) Access RPPR from the RPPR module by selecting the specific grant on the Manage RPPR screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOs/AOs must perform a query first in the RPPR module. The appropriate RPPR Menu screen (single- or multi-project) displays with editing options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing and editing Human Subjects (HSS/HSCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs or signing officials (SOs) can access the Human Subjects System (HSS) / HSCT form using the Human Subjects links in either the RPPR or the Status screen in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human Subjects information may need to be updated post-award for RPPR updates (including inclusion enrollment and Clinical Trial Milestone Plan), pre-award (post review) for JIT, off-cycle updates as required in the FOA or terms, or corrections to human subject data. To edit an existing study, access the HSCT Post Submission tab; study record must be in Work in Progress status to edit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Inclusion Enrollment Report (IER) cumulative counts
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two ways to edit the existing Inclusion Enrollment Report (IER) data for Cumulative (Actual) counts: (1) update the cells online in the existing report, or (2) download a spreadsheet template for entering participant-level data and upload it to populate the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uploading, use the provided CSV template (Download Participant Level Data Template), fill it, save, then upload via Upload Participant Level Data Attachment to update cumulative counts. You can also download current participant level data for records. Notes: must use the template if uploading; individual-level participant data on characteristics at enrollment will be required in-progress reports for competitive applications submitted for due dates on or after January 25, 2019 (NOT-OD-18-116).

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned counts update method
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Planned counts, the cells must be updated online in the report itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned counts cannot be updated via the participant-level template upload; they are entered directly in the RPPR online form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview Study feature
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire study can be previewed before submission by clicking the Preview Study button on the left navigational column under Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preview to confirm how study data will appear prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving and locking behavior for PI and SO when editing studies
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PI is making changes: the PI can click the Save and Release Lock button to save changes; submission status changes to Work in Progress; PI changes status to Ready for Submission. If the SO is making changes: the SO can click the Save and Keep Lock button to save changes; submission status changes to Work in Progress; SO changes status to Ready for Submission; the Submit action becomes active on the Application Information page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless an SO has delegated Submit authority to the contact PI, only the SO can submit the application to NIH. The submission sends all updated study records associated with the application to NIH at one time. Program officials and grant specialists are notified automatically of study changes. Some changes may require prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing single-project RPPR for editing
rubrics_metrics.description: For single-project awards, on the RPPR Menu screen click the three-dot ellipsis icon and select Edit RPPR to open the RPPR for editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Once an RPPR has been routed for review, the Recall button is enabled. Refer to Editing the RPPR Forms for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project RPPR - component reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-project awards, each component must be reported in the RPPR. A component is a distinct, reviewable part of the multi-project application or progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components typically include general information, performance sites, personnel, and budget. The FOA defines construction and naming; funded application defines construction for the progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding individual components (existing or new)
rubrics_metrics.description: To add components if none are displayed, select Yes on Has components? and use Add Component to select Existing App Component or New Component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To add from list: Select from existing App Components, choose component and Add Component. To add manually: enter Component Project Title, select Component Project Type, click Add Component. Components added appear in component table and can be edited via ellipsis -> Edit RPPR. Any previously added components will be displayed and Has components? may be disabled. Components are pulled from the beginning of segment award of the last completing application plus manually entered components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deleting components - irreversible loss
rubrics_metrics.description: You can delete added components, but you cannot delete the Overall component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMPORTANT: If you choose to delete a component, all data related to this component – including all budget data – will be lost. This data cannot be recovered once it has been deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for RPPR errors (component or overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: To check for RPPR errors on either the Overall component or an individual component, click its three-dot ellipsis icon and select Check for Errors. Errors will be displayed at the top of the screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors must be corrected to submit. Warnings are displayed but submission may proceed depending on type (see submission guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing the RPPR - process and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reports in Work in Progress (WIP) status can be routed to others for review or corrections by the current reviewer of the report. The routing feature is on the RPPR Menu screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To route: select Route to Next Reviewer, choose next reviewer from dropdown, optional comments, Required for PD/PI ONLY: click checkbox that certifies statements are true (Signing officials do not see this checkbox), then click Route to Next Reviewer. A successful routing message appears. The person who routed can no longer edit the report; editing becomes available only to the new reviewer. RPPR status updates to Reviewer Work in Progress. Note: a person delegated ASST cannot route an RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR routing history - audit trail
rubrics_metrics.description: From initiation to submission to the agency, the routing of an RPPR is captured for auditing purposes. PD/PIs, PD/PI delegates, and reviewers can view the routing history for Work in Progress or Submitted to Agency RPPRs at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To view: ellipsis -> View Routing History; close the screen via Close link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing RPPR as PDF - recommended pre-submission check
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees are strongly encouraged to view the RPPR as a PDF prior to submission to ensure that the correct information and attachments are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD/PIs, PD/PI delegates, and reviewers can view a PDF version of an RPPR in Work in Progress (WIP) or Submitted to Agency status. Until submitted, the PDF shows status Draft and a blank submission date. To view: ellipsis -> View RPPR as PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting RPPR to agency - who may submit and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed and validated RPPRs in a status of Work in Progress can be submitted to the agency for acceptance. The signing official (SO) can submit when the SO is the current reviewer; PD/PIs may submit for SNAP awards if delegated; delegation of RPPR privileges not allowed on DOC awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit: ellipsis -> Submit. The Submit RPPR screen displays a certification statement which the SO (or delegated PD/PI) must accept via I Agree. Certification affirms compliance with Notice of Award and Grants Policy, verifies accuracy, and warns of consequences (withdrawal, suspension, termination, debarment, criminal penalties, reimbursement) for falsification or misrepresentation. NOTE: A PD/PI with Progress Report authority cannot submit a non-SNAP or F RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation, errors and warnings at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: On submission the RPPR is validated for system and business rules. Validation failures are indicated by error messages on the RPPR Menu screen and must be corrected to submit. Warnings are displayed but the RPPR can be submitted with warnings present after review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If warnings exist: Cancel to correct and resubmit or OK to continue despite warnings. If all validations pass, a success message displays: 'The RPPR has been successfully submitted to PHS,' current reviewer updates to awarding agency, status updates to Submitted to Agency, and submission date recorded. Associated publications in C.1 are linked to MyNCBI; inclusion enrollment data are updated into eRA inclusion data system as data of record; email notifications sent to PD/PI, SO, and AO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project submission errors/warnings display rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission, multi-project RPPRs are validated like single-projects but errors and warnings are displayed differently: Overall messages are shown first followed by messages for other components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All errors must be corrected to submit. Warnings are displayed under errors. Although the RPPR can be submitted with warnings, review the warning messages to determine if issues should be addressed. A sample of possible error messages is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalling the RPPR - who can recall and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPRs that have been routed to a reviewer can be recalled by the person who performed the routing action. The last reviewer can recall; signing officials and the Contact PD/PI (who are not the last reviewer) can also recall when the report is in Reviewer Work in Progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: A person who has been delegated the PD/PI role does not have the ability to recall the RPPR. To recall: ellipsis -> Recall. A message displays confirming recall; you become the current reviewer; status updates to PD/PI Work in Progress or Reviewer Work in Progress; the reviewer from whom it is recalled receives an email; routing audit history updated; Edit RPPR and Route to Next Reviewer options restored for the new reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim and Final RPPR timing and when required
rubrics_metrics.description: As of January 1, 2017, a Final RPPR is required for any grant that has ended and any grant that is not to be extended through award of a new competitive segment; the report is due within 120 days of the end of the project period. Effective February 9, 2017, if the recipient organization has submitted a renewal application on or before the date a Final RPPR would be required, an Interim RPPR is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim RPPR is used for submission of a Competing Renewal application (Type 2). Both Interim and Final RPPR are identical in process and information; differences vs annual RPPR: in Interim/Final only D.1 required in Participants, Sections F and H are not part of Interim/Final, Section I Outcomes is required for Interim/Final. If a system check fails to detect pending renewal, an Interim RPPR may be converted to Final RPPR in Closeout. See Guide Notices NOT-OD-17-022 and NOT-OD-17-037.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-specific RPPR applicability and special instructions (AHRQ, VA, DOC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain agencies have specific RPPR requirements: AHRQ grantees are required to use eRA Commons RPPR module and follow HHS Grants Policy Statement Prior Approval Requirements for significant changes; DOC has exceptions (e.g., Interim RPPRs not applicable); VA-ORD requires progress reports each budget year within competitive segment, Interim reports when project period over and renewal pending, Final reports for ended awards not renewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VA-ORD: outcomes are not published and VA-ORD has specific reporting content that differs from NIH template; guidance links provided. DOC: some sections/forms not applicable; SNAP and DOC delegation rules differ. Refer to agency-specific links and RPPR Instruction Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting Interim RPPR - availability and steps
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit an Interim RPPR: click the Interim RPPR link for the grant from Status search results (the link appears for PI and SO one day after budget period end date and before award moves to Closeout), click Initiate to create Interim RPPR, then Edit RPPR and complete each section as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sure to click SAVE when moving between sections or unsaved data may be lost. Interim RPPR Menu has same ellipsis actions as Final RPPR Menu. The Interim RPPR link is available when grant is eligible for Competing Renewal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Report Additional Materials (IRAM) - agency requests and response process
rubrics_metrics.description: The awarding agency might issue an Interim Report Additional Materials (IRAM) request following submission of an Interim RPPR to request additional information. This lets the awardee enter, review, and submit information in response to a specific request from the program official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either the PI or SO (or their delegates) can upload files and provide a revised project outcome in response to an IRAM. For a multi-PI project, the contact PI can respond to the IRAM, but only an SO can submit the IRAM package to the agency. Agency-specific note: IRAMs are not applicable for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised Outcomes via IRAM - how to submit revised text
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit revised project outcomes in response to an IRAM, enter text in the Revised Outcome text box on the IRAM screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the instructions at the top of the IRAM screen. Click the Save button at bottom of screen to save entered text.
